name: AgentDojo
description: AgentDojo is an open-source dynamic evaluation framework designed to assess the adversarial robustness of AI agents that interact with external tools and plugins. It simulates realistic agentic task environments (e-banking, email, travel booking, team messaging) in which adversarial prompt injections are embedded in tool outputs.

metadata.description: AgentDojo is an open-source dynamic evaluation framework designed to assess the adversarial robustness of AI agents that interact with external tools and plugins. It simulates realistic agentic task environments (e-banking, email, travel booking, team messaging) in which adversarial prompt injections are embedded in tool outputs.
metadata.scientific_reference: Debenedetti, E., et al. (2024). AgentDojo. NeurIPS 2024. https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13352
metadata.project_maturity: Research benchmark published at NeurIPS 2024; actively maintained and extended by US and UK AI Safety Institutes
metadata.target_legal_requirements: EU AI Act – Article 15 (Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity)
metadata.input_spec: Configuration arguments defining a benchmark run: suite, model, attack, defense, and task.
metadata.config_params:
- suite (String, banking, slack, travel, workspace): Task environment/domain to benchmark.
- user_task (String): Specific user task(s) to evaluate.
- model (String): LLM to test as the agent. 25+ supported models.
- defense (String, none, tool_filter, repeat_user_prompt, transformers_pi_detector, spotlighting_with_delimiting): Protection mechanism applied to the agent.
- attack (String, none, important_instructions, direct, ignore_previous, tool_knowledge, injecagent, dos, and variants): Prompt injection strategy.
- injection_task (String): Adversarial goal for attack scenarios.
- benchmark_version (String, v1.2.2, v1.2.1, or custom): Benchmark specification version.
- logdir (Path): Directory to save JSON result files.
- tool_output_format (String, yaml, json): Serialization format for tool responses.
- force_rerun (Boolean): Overwrite existing logs for the same configuration.
metadata.additional_output_fields: suite, user_task, injection_task, attack, defense, model, benchmark_version, messages, system_message
metadata.contextual_guidance: Baseline utility above 70% indicates strong capability. Security rate above 50% indicates meaningful injection resistance. ASR above 80% indicates highly effective attack.
metadata.visualisation: Utility-vs-security scatter plot; attack effectiveness heatmap; suite-level comparison bar chart; defense comparison table
metadata.reporting: Report should highlight baseline utility rate per model and suite, security rate under attack, and attack success rate across all tested combinations.

metrics.name: utility
metrics.represents: Whether the agent successfully completed the user task.

metrics.name: security
metrics.represents: Whether the agent resisted the prompt injection attack.

metrics.name: duration
metrics.represents: Wall-clock time from task start to completion.

metrics.name: message_count
metrics.represents: Number of messages exchanged with the LLM.

metrics.name: tool_call_count
metrics.represents: Number of tool invocations made by the agent.

name: LangBiTe
description: LangBiTe is an open-source bias testing framework for large language models. Given a user-defined ethical requirements model specifying ethical concerns (e.g. sexism, racism, ageism) and sensitive communities (e.g. gender groups, ethnic groups, age groups), LangBiTe automatically selects prompt templates from a curated library, generates test case variants for each community, executes them against one or more LLMs, evaluates the responses using test oracles, and produces evaluation reports with end-to-end traceability between ethical requirements and assessment results. The framework includes prompt template libraries with 300+ templates in English, Spanish, and Catalan covering sexism/misogyny, racism, xenophobia, ageism, political bias, LGTBIQ+phobia, and religious discrimination.

metadata.description: LangBiTe is an open-source bias testing framework for large language models. Given a user-defined ethical requirements model specifying ethical concerns (e.g. sexism, racism, ageism) and sensitive communities (e.g. gender groups, ethnic groups, age groups), LangBiTe automatically selects prompt templates from a curated library, generates test case variants for each community, executes them against one or more LLMs, evaluates the responses using test oracles, and produces evaluation reports with end-to-end traceability between ethical requirements and assessment results. The framework includes prompt template libraries with 300+ templates in English, Spanish, and Catalan covering sexism/misogyny, racism, xenophobia, ageism, political bias, LGTBIQ+phobia, and religious discrimination.
metadata.provider: SOM Research Lab, Universitat Oberta de Catalunya (UOC)
metadata.scientific_reference: Morales, S., Clarisó, R., & Cabot, J. (2024). A DSL for testing LLMs for fairness and bias. ACM/IEEE MODELS '24. https://doi.org/10.1145/3640310.3674093
metadata.project_maturity: Actively maintained research framework; primary publication at ACM/IEEE MODELS 2024
metadata.target_legal_requirements: EU AI Act – Article 10 (Data and data governance, non-discrimination)
metadata.input_spec:
Inputs are an ethical requirements model and a test scenario definition, provided as a JSON object or JSON file.
sampleTypes: ethical requirements model, test scenario definition
formats: JSON object, JSON file
metadata.config_params:
- ethical_concerns (List of objects): Ethical concerns to evaluate and their associated sensitive communities.
- llms (List of objects): Target LLMs to evaluate. Supported providers: OpenAI, HuggingFace, Replicate.
- num_templates (Integer, >= 1): Number of prompt templates to retrieve per ethical concern.
- temperature (Float, 0.0–2.0): Temperature parameter for LLM inference.
- max_tokens (Integer, >= 1): Maximum number of tokens for LLM response generation.
- num_retries (Integer, >= 1): Number of times each prompt is executed against the LLM.
- language (String, en, es, ca): Language of the prompt template library.
- useLLMEval (Boolean, true / false): Whether to use a second LLM as judge to re-evaluate failed test cases.
- eval_llm (Object): The second LLM used for LLM-as-a-judge re-evaluation.
- prompt_library (String): Custom prompt template library CSV path. If omitted, built-in library is used.
metadata.additional_output_fields: ethical_concern, community, prompt_template, instantiated_prompt, llm_response, provider, model, oracle_type, oracle_expected, oracle_result, llm_eval_result
metadata.contextual_guidance: A global pass rate above 75% indicates acceptable performance; below 25% indicates severe and widespread bias.
metadata.visualisation: Pass rate bar chart per ethical concern per LLM; Community divergence heatmap; LLM comparison radar chart
metadata.reporting: Report should highlight global pass rate per LLM and per ethical concern, communities most frequently subjected to differential treatment, and proportion of oracle failures per bias category.

metrics.name: pass
metrics.represents: Whether the LLM response passed the oracle evaluation.

metrics.name: pass_rate
metrics.represents: Proportion of test cases that passed, aggregated per ethical concern, LLM, or globally.

metadata.scientific_reference: Khan, M. A., et al. (2024). A comprehensive assessment tool for prompt injection attacks in LLMs. IEEE. https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/11395844

metadata.input_spec:
Configuration files (YAML/JSON) defining prompts, models, test cases, and evaluation criteria. Two modes: basic evaluation and red team.
formats: YAML, JSON, JavaScript
metadata.config_params:
- description (String): Human-readable evaluation suite name.
- prompts (List of strings): Prompt templates with {{var}} placeholders.
- providers (List of strings/objects): LLM models to test. Format: {service}:{type}:{model}.
- tests (List of objects): Test cases with vars and assert criteria. Basic mode only.
- redteam (Object): Configuration for adversarial testing.
- redteam.plugins (List of strings/objects): Security frameworks: owasp:llm, harmful, nist:ai:measure, gdpr, eu:ai-act.
- redteam.numTests (Integer, >= 1): Adversarial prompts generated per plugin.
- redteam.strategies (List of strings, [], [jailbreak], [prompt-injection]): Attack transformations.
- redteam.language (String): ISO 639-1 language code for test generation.
- maxConcurrency (Integer, >= 1): Max concurrent LLM requests.
- cache (Boolean/object): Enable LLM response caching.
metadata.additional_output_fields: evalId, timestamp, promptfooVersion, config, metadata.pluginId, metadata.harmCategory, metadata.severity, metadata.framework
metadata.contextual_guidance: Red team pass rate > 95% = excellent security. < 50% = severe vulnerabilities, block deployment.
metadata.visualisation: Pass rate bar chart; plugin vulnerability heatmap; latency vs cost scatter plot; provider comparison table
metadata.reporting: Report should highlight overall pass rate per provider and per security plugin, vulnerability categories most frequently exploited, and distribution of scores.

metadata.input_spec:
Two datasets: a reference dataset (baseline to establish constraints, e.g. training data) and an evaluated dataset (checked for anomalies, e.g. testing data).

metadata.input_spec:
Two datasets: a reference dataset (baseline, e.g. training data) and an evaluated dataset (e.g. testing data). A human-validation time feature is required in both datasets to simulate drift over time.
formats: dataset

- target_feature (str): The name of the target feature, selected from the dataset features.
- date_feature (str): The name of the date feature indicating the time of human decision, selected from the dataset features.
- features (List of feature objects): Each feature object is composed of name (str), min (float), max (float) and feature type (enum).

metrics.name: ratio_features_with_drift
